about: The Remem Test (the delayed test) for every concept the question generator has produced for a ready-made topic: three unseen questions per concept, written to one rubric. kind: use = a new situation where the idea is applied; explain = why it happens or what follows; apart = tell it from a neighbouring idea, put steps in order, or work something out. They replace the generator's 5th question and are added as the 6th and 7th (backend.remem_test_upgrade).

Origin of Hangul.stem: What did Hangul most likely make easier for ordinary Koreans?
Hangul was created in 1443 but announced in 1446. What does that tell you?
options: It existed for a few years before it was made public
It was created by two different kings
It was announced before it was finished

Origin of Hangul.stem: Counting to 2026, about how long ago was Hangul created?

Hangul Structure.stem: A Korean word has two syllables. How is it written in Hangul?
options: As one long line of letters
As two square blocks side by side

Hangul Structure.stem: Why can a short Hangul word contain more letters than blocks?
options: Each block packs the letters of one syllable together
Some letters are silent and not written
Blocks are only used for names
Vowels are written outside the blocks

Hangul Structure.stem: How many more basic consonants than basic vowels does Hangul have?

Functions of the Silent ㅇ.stem: Why is ㅇ written in 아 even though it makes no sound there?
options: A syllable block has to start with a consonant
It shows the word is a name

Functions of the Silent ㅇ.stem: In 앙, how are the two ㅇ letters pronounced?

Double Consonants.stem: Which syllable starts with a double consonant?
How does ㄲ differ from ㅋ?
options: ㄲ is silent and ㅋ sounds like k
ㄲ is a tense double sound; ㅋ has a puff of breath
ㄲ has a puff of breath; ㅋ is tense

Double Consonants.stem: Which pair shows a consonant and its double form?

Exposure Balancing.stem: You open the aperture from f/4 to f/2.8 (one stop). To keep the same exposure, what could you change?
options: Use a shutter speed twice as slow
Use a shutter speed twice as fast

Exposure Balancing.stem: Why might a sports photographer raise the ISO at an indoor game?
options: To use a fast shutter that freezes motion and still get a bright photo

Exposure Balancing.stem: Starting at ISO 100, how many stops brighter is ISO 800?

Composition and Light.stem: Indoors under yellow bulbs, white paper looks yellow in your photo. Which setting is meant to fix this?
Which landscape photo follows the rule of thirds?
options: A horizon exactly across the middle
A subject cut off at the edge
A horizon along the lower third line of the frame
A subject filling the whole frame

Composition and Light.stem: Sunrise is at 6:00 and sunset at 18:30. Which time is in golden hour?

Uzbekistan's Geography and Culture.stem: Travelling from Uzbekistan to the open sea, at least how many borders must you cross?
Which two countries both use a currency called the som?
A traveller visits Samarkand, then flies to that country's capital. Where do they land?

Tajikistan's Geography and Language.stem: Someone pays in somoni in Dushanbe, near the Pamir Mountains. Which country are they in?

options: Tajikistan uses the som, Kyrgyzstan the somoni
Tajikistan uses the somoni, Kyrgyzstan the som

Tajikistan's Geography and Language.stem: Which description fits Tajikistan rather than Turkmenistan?
options: Mostly mountains, with a language close to Persian
Has the Gates of Hell crater

Turkmenistan's Features.stem: A traveller pays in manat and visits a gas crater that has burned for decades. Which country are they in?
Which word best describes most of Turkmenistan's land?
By 2025, about how long had the Darvaza gas crater been burning?

Confirmation bias.stem: A manager decides a new employee is lazy. Over a month she notices every late arrival but none of the extra hours. What is going on?
Which habit protects you best against confirmation bias?
options: Looking for evidence that could prove you wrong

Confirmation bias.stem: Sam remembers only the stories that agree with his view of a politician. Neha fears sharks after one news story. Which one shows confirmation bias?

Sunk cost fallacy.stem: Asha keeps going to a gym she hates only because she paid for the whole year. Which bias is this?
A company has spent 2 crore rupees on a failing project. What should decide whether it carries on?
options: How long they have worked on it
Whether finishing it will bring more benefit from now on than it costs

Sunk cost fallacy.stem: Which choice is NOT the sunk cost fallacy?
options: Finishing a meal you dislike because you paid for it
Leaving a boring film because the rest of your evening is worth more
Staying in a course you hate because of the fees already paid
Repairing an old car again because you have spent so much on it

Availability heuristic.stem: After several news stories about shark attacks, Riya thinks swimming in the sea is very dangerous. Which idea explains this?
How could you correct for the availability heuristic when judging a risk?
options: Rely on the most recent news story
Ask a friend who was affected
Check how often it actually happens, not how easily examples come to mind

Availability heuristic.stem: After seeing one lottery winner on the news, Dev thinks winning is likely. Mira remembers only the times her horoscope was right. Who shows the availability heuristic?

Dunning-Kruger effect.stem: After one week of chess lessons, Arjun is sure he could beat most club players. Which effect does this show?
Which would help most someone showing the Dunning-Kruger effect?
options: A clear test that shows them their own mistakes

Dunning-Kruger effect.stem: After one guitar lesson Rohan says he plays better than most people; Priya, a concert pianist, assumes others play as well as she does. Which is right?

Framing effect.stem: A shop says 'Save 20 percent today' instead of 'Pay 80 percent of the price'. The deal is the same. Which effect makes the first sound better?
Two adverts describe the same loan as '95 percent approved' and '5 percent rejected'. Most people prefer the first. Why?
options: The same facts feel different in a gain frame

Framing effect.stem: Which pair describes the same facts, once in a gain frame and once in a loss frame?

GPS Receiver Functionality.stem: Why can any number of phones use GPS at the same time?
options: Each phone has its own satellite
Only a few phones can use it at once
The satellites broadcast and receivers only listen, so phones add no load

GPS Receiver Functionality.stem: What does a phone need from each satellite to work out its position?
options: A reply to a message the phone sent
The satellite's position and the exact time its signal was sent

GPS Receiver Functionality.stem: A signal travels at the speed of light and takes about 0.07 seconds to arrive. About how far away is the satellite?

Necessity of Four Satellites.stem: A receiver's clock is 1 millisecond fast. About how wrong would its distances be if nothing corrected it?
Why can phones use a cheap clock instead of an atomic one?
options: Phones get atomic time from the mobile network
The fourth satellite's signal lets the receiver work out its own clock error
Cheap clocks are just as accurate
The satellites correct each phone's clock directly
Satellite sends its position and time, receiver notes the arrival time, works out distances, then solves for position and clock error
Receiver works out distances, satellite sends time, receiver notes arrival, then solves
Receiver solves for position, notes arrival time, satellite sends time, then works out distances
Satellite sends time, receiver solves for position, notes arrival, then works out distances

Relativistic Clock Corrections.stem: Without any correction, about how much time would a satellite clock gain on ground clocks over 10 days?
Why does a clock error of only 38 microseconds a day matter for GPS?
options: Light travels so far in that time that positions would be off by kilometres

Relativistic Clock Corrections.stem: If the relativity correction were switched off, about how far off would positions be after one week?

Navigation Systems and Accuracy.stem: Between tall office buildings your map shows you 40 metres from where you really are. What is the likely reason?
options: The satellites are switched off in cities
Too many people are using GPS
The buildings block or reflect the satellite signals

Navigation Systems and Accuracy.stem: Which of these is a regional system rather than a global one?
Where is a phone's GPS likely to be most accurate?
options: In an open field under a clear sky

Serving Size.stem: Crisps A: 150 kcal per 30 g serving. Crisps B: 520 kcal per 100 g. Which has more energy per gram?
options: You can't tell from the labels

Serving Size.stem: Two snacks both say '120 kcal per serving'. Why might one give you far more energy when you finish the pack?
options: Their serving sizes and servings per pack can differ
kcal are measured differently by each brand

Serving Size.stem: A 3-serving pack lists 4 g of sugar per serving. You eat two-thirds of the pack. How much sugar is that?

Percent Daily Value.stem: Cereal A gives 4 percent of the daily value of fibre per serving; cereal B gives 22 percent. Which is the high-fibre choice?
A cereal gives 10 percent of the daily value of fibre per serving. You eat two servings. How is your fibre from it described?
Why is percent daily value more useful than grams for judging whether a food is high in a nutrient?
options: It is always a smaller number
It shows the amount against what you need in a whole day
